newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Bourses mixed, dollar marks time before data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bourses mixed, dollar marks time before data.

text.p: European bourses traded mixed and the dollar was steady on Thursday, with only a mildly bullish German economic forecast stirring the waters ahead of the annual summit of leading industrialised nations that starts on Friday.

Trade relations between the U.S. and Japan remained the focus of the foreign exchange market, with traders looking for signs of friction at the Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Denver following a surge in Japan's trade and current account surpluses.
German shares bucked the early European trend and rose, although dealers said the market was largely driven by technical factors ahead of Friday's "triple witching" of futures and options contracts.
The Ifo economic institute reported that German business confidence was slightly higher than expected in May and said it believed Europe's powerhouse economy could still qualify for monetary union.
It forecast German gross domestic product would grow between 2.0 and 2.5 percent in 1997 but the average number of unemployed would rise by more than 300,000 to 4.3 million.
"The numbers support the view that the economic recovery is on track and that the economy is poised for expansion," said Armin Kayser, economist at Swiss Bank Corp in Frankfurt.
By 1115 GMT the 30-share DAX index was off its highs but still showing gains of 0.42 percent at 3,746 points.
Volkswagen rose 25.2 marks to 1,245, driven by derivatives business and market expectations of what would emerge from its annual general meeting.
Europe's other two major bourses in London and Paris both declined in early trade, but Paris later recovered to just above Wednesday's closing level.
French dealers said they were waiting for direction from new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's keynote policy speech to parliament in the afternoon.
"The bourse is holding up. People hope it'll be a moderate message," a broker said. "We're just waiting. It's very calm."
The CAC-40 index was up 3.77 points at 2,755 by 1115 GMT, having hit a low of 2,734 during the morning.
Like Frankfurt, the London share market was heavily influenced by derivatives ahead of Friday's futures and options expiry.

Also weighing on the market were worries about next month's budget and news of an 11.1 percent year-on-year rise in M4 money supply in May, which reinforced fears of another rise in interest rates following Wednesday's strong retail sales figures.

"The figures today are going to be damaging to the gilt markets with such strong lending on the back of strong retail sales numbers. It is certainly going to put upward pressure on inflation expectations," Nikko economist Simon Briscoe said.
"It is now quite likely that base rates will rise in July unless the budget is especially tough on the personal sector."
By mid-session the blue chip FTSE 100 index was down 22.8 points at 4,634.2.

Potential U.S.-Japan trade friction remained the main focus of the foreign exchange market ahead of a U.S. trade report due out at 1230 GMT and the start of the annual Group of Seven (G7) summit in Denver on Friday.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said overnight that leaders from the G7 leading industrial nations would discuss the risk that further significant increases in Japan's trade surpluses could undermine growth in other countries and trigger a backlash against trade liberalisation.
His comments followed a Japanese report on Wednesday that showed Japan's trade surplus with the United States and other countries surged in May.

"No one wants to go short ahead of the G7 but given that Japan's trade surpluses will continue to rise in the next quarter or two, there will be downward pressure on dollar/yen," said Paul Megyessi, strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7309 marks and 113.30 yen, compared with 1.7289 and 113.32 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1115 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 22.8 points, or 0.49 percent, at 4,634.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 3.77 points, or 0.14 percent, at 2,755.51.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 15.82 points, or 0.42 percent, at 3,746.09.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $340.15 against $341.60 on Wednesday. Silver was unchanged at $4.73. Platinum was up $10.50 at $420.00, palladium rose $15.00 to $206.50.
